correctness.rationale: Summing over the free high digit forces u divisible by p. For a unit v the remaining p exponents have distinct low digits, so their count polynomial cannot be divisible by the prime-square cyclotomic polynomial; for v=pV the geometric sum is zero exactly for U+V nonzero. In each low first-digit block, pairwise orthogonality therefore fixes the low second digit and requires distinct high-digit sums. A basis fills all p blocks and all p sums per block. The functions and counts are forced. A subgroup supporting an affine spectrum must have a unit first-coordinate projection, hence is a cyclic slope graph; slopes not congruent to -1 give exactly p^4-p^3 affine spectra with their intercepts. The Frobenius specialization follows by binomial expansion modulo p^2. The recorded finite checks are corroboration only and the uploaded code was not executed.

originality.rationale: A distinct indexed result covers the entire finding, not just the Frobenius specialization or the existence of a basis. For each h put g(r)=h(r)-(r^p-r)/p modulo p. Then the indexed E_g and frozen S_h are exactly the same point set in the same coordinates, and the correspondence of functions is bijective. The indexed zero set, unique basis parametrization and both counts agree. This is demonstrated equivalent coverage as of review, not an assertion that the indexed November 2 record has priority over the frozen October 19 record or that the latter was derivative.
